# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

# Agent guide

Rules for AI agents working in this repo.

## Crates

| Crate | License | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| callisto-model | MIT | none |
| callisto-manifests | FSL-1.1-MIT | model |
| callisto-graph | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests |
| callisto-cli | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph |
| callisto-fixtures | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) |

- `callisto-model` (MIT) must never depend on an FSL crate.
- Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml` after adding or moving a crate.

## Commands

- Full pipeline: `just ci` (includes the 90% coverage gate). `just test`, `just lint`, `just fmt`.
- Scoped iteration: one `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` at a time.
  - Not `moon run <project>:test`: its per-project fan-out serializes on `target/`'s build lock.
  - Never run cargo builds in parallel.
- Changesets: `callisto add --package callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` (non-interactive). Target `callisto-cli`: its changelog is the one users read. One changeset per user-visible topic, written as the changelog entry: what the user sees now, no internal names or mechanism.
- Never `git checkout -- Cargo.lock` as cleanup. A lockfile diff means investigate, not discard.

## Invariants

1. Safe Rust only: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
2. Manifest edits preserve format: `toml_edit` for TOML; JSON keeps key order and fingerprinted indentation. No regex or line edits.
3. File writes go through `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write`.
4. User-facing errors derive `miette::Diagnostic` with a code and a fix.
5. No emojis in docs or code.
6. No cargo features in shipped crates; behaviour is chosen at runtime (#143). The dev-only `callisto-model/test-util` feature is the exception.

## Fixing bugs

- Grep for structurally identical code (same algorithm, other file, ecosystem or mode). A sibling with the same defect is in scope now.
- N copies of one logic: unify to one implementation rather than patching each.
- A deliberately deferred sibling gets an explicit record: changeset note, tracked follow-up or code comment.
- A new shared helper migrates every call site in the same change, or the rest are tracked.

## Specs and plans

- Specs (`spec@1`) live in `docs/specs/`, one per area, current behavior only. Change the spec in the same PR as the behavior. No history, rationale or revision notes.
- This repo's release workflow has no GitHub Environment or reviewer gate and only `execute` gets registry secrets (owner policy, enforced by `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh`). Never add one.
- Read `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the matching `docs/architecture/` topic before changing behavior in an area.
- Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing release flow, Git access, publishing, distribution, platform packages or manifest writes. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR the owner accepts.
- Plans (`plan@1`) live in `docs/projects/`. Delete a plan once its work ships.
- Code never cites specs: no spec IDs, criterion IDs, section numbers or track names in comments, test names or messages. Describe the behavior instead.
- A requirement the owner didn't state is a judgment call. Get owner confirmation before it gates anything.

## Writing

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown or PR bodies: one line per paragraph.
- Code comments: one short line, only for a non-obvious why. Wrap at 120 columns (`rustfmt.toml`). No history ("used to", "previously"): git records it.
- No claude.ai session links in commits, PRs or files.

- [Post-0.10.2 Plan](project_post_0_10_2_plan.md) — Open work after the 0.10.2 release lives in .claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md (local only, never PR it): 12 workstreams, parallel lanes, stacked PRs, owner decisions (D01 blocks MATURIN/OWNER).

- [Iterate Reviews in Foreground](feedback_iterate_reviews_in_foreground.md) — Background agent notifications were unreliable across a multi-round spec/plan review loop; user called it out twice — run tight revise-review cycles in the foreground.

- [Always Use Plugins](feedback_always_use_plugins.md) — Route PR/commit narration and audits through courier/ranger/etc. plugin agents by default, not freehand, even when I already have full context.
- [Terse Comments Only](feedback_terse_comments.md) — One short line max, only for non-obvious WHY; stop writing multi-line prose comments in code/config even though CLAUDE.md already says this.
- [Cargo Slowness Root Cause](project_cargo_slowness_target_pollution.md) — Hours-long builds were a polluted target/debug (1.7M .o files); wipe it, split-debuginfo=off, one invocation shape, no parallel builds; cold build is 31 s.
- [No Red-Green, Lean Tokens](feedback_no_red_green_lean_tokens.md) — User dropped red-green testing and wants lean token spend; no heavy agent gating loops; CLI product tag callisto@{version} is intentional.
- [PR #101 Hardening State](project_pr101_hardening_state.md) — 7 local unpushed commits fix the audited release-lifecycle defects; deferred structural work, unverified-on-GitHub items, and the git add -u lesson.
- [Never Hard-Wrap Prose](feedback_never_hard_wrap_prose.md) — PR descriptions and all Markdown: one line per paragraph, never manual line breaks.
- [Succinct Written Artifacts](feedback_succinct_written_artifacts.md) — Changesets, PR bodies, docs: short, plain, no AI slop or backstory.
- [No Session Links](feedback_no_session_links.md) — Never put claude.ai session URLs/Claude-Session trailers in commits or PRs; public repo, private sessions.
- [Verify Before Recommending](feedback_verify_before_recommending.md) — Check code, callers and sibling repos before presenting any recommendation; audit findings are leads, not conclusions.
- [No Thin ADRs](feedback_no_thin_adrs.md) — ADRs only for significant decisions, with rejected options, enforcement and revisit triggers; process rules aren't ADRs.
- [Budget: Lean Pipeline](feedback_budget_lean_pipeline.md) — weekly token budget; leanest pipeline that still catches bugs; no cleanup agents or rework the user has to review.
- [Use gh stack](feedback_use_gh_stack.md) — stacked PRs must be native GitHub stacks (gh stack link); plain chained PRs get no CI.
- [Agent Context Briefs](feedback_agent_context_briefs.md) — curated 2-4k token briefs, one agent per PR via SendMessage, small fixes directly; no forks of long sessions.
- [Local Tracking, Not PRs](feedback_local_tracking_not_prs.md) — Tracking/handoff plans live in .claude/plans/ (git-excluded); never commit or PR them (PR #201 was closed for this).

Review of the uncommitted sealed-Python-set change in pypi-sealed-set. I found no way to upload bytes other than the sealed ones when a valid manifest is supplied. I found two weakenings of the "strict" claim (F1, F2), one silent opt-out (F3) and two minor edges (F4, F5). I read the code only and ran nothing.

**Findings (none is a hard bypass of a correctly produced manifest)**

**F1. Sealed bytes are verified once, then trusted at upload (Medium, CONFIRMED by trace).**
- `release_artifacts.rs:139-153` hashes the files at the start of `execute`.
- `registry.rs:916-960` (`publish`) uploads `file.path` and never re-hashes.
- Between the two, the executor runs earlier operations, including propagation waits and retries. The sealed `BuiltFile.sha256` comes from the manifest, not from the file on disk.
- Failing scenario: a file in `release-assets` is swapped or edited after verification, and twine uploads the new bytes.
- The only detector is `confirm` (`registry.rs:975-1011`), which runs after the irreversible upload and only fires if the index serves a sha256 (F2).
- Fix: re-hash and re-check for symlinks inside `publish` right before building the upload argv. Alternatively, copy the verified files into a private temp dir at verify time.

**F2. A missing sha256 passes the strict compare as "equal" (Low-Medium, CONFIRMED).**
- `pypi_files.rs:221-224` uses `held.sha256().is_some_and(|d| d != file.sha256)`. An index entry with no `sha256` key never counts as differing. PEP 691 only requires some hash, so an index that serves only sha512 qualifies.
- For a sealed set, a same-name file with unknown bytes is accepted as `AlreadySatisfied` in preflight and as exact in `confirm`. That contradicts the sealed guarantee.
- Fix: for a sealed set, treat a missing sha256 as Indeterminate or as differing.

**F3. Sealing is opt-in on the execute side (Medium as a design gap).**
- `validate_distributions` (`artifact.rs:282`) accepts an empty list. Nothing in the intent or envelope requires a seal.
- Scenario 1: an intent with slots and a Python publish, with a manifest from `artifact-manifest` run without `--seal-python`. `built_set` (`registry.rs:766-795`) falls back to building in the credentialed job, with only an `eprintln` warning.
- Scenario 2: a Python-only intent run with no `--artifact-manifest` gets `(true, None, None) => None` in `release.rs:~570`. It builds silently, with no warning at all.
- Scenario 3: the generated workflow's `has_python` switch is the only thing that turns sealing on. A stale or edited workflow downgrades the release with no error.
- Fix: make the execute-side requirement explicit, for example a `--require-sealed-python` flag, or record sealing in the intent or envelope. If the opt-out is intentional, it needs a record under AGENTS.md ("deliberately deferred" rule).

**F4. Execute never checks that sealed filenames belong to the package and version (Low, PLAUSIBLE, defense in depth).**
- Only `inventory` filters by name and version, and only at seal time.
- `validate_distributions` and `sealed_files` check just safe component names, one wheel, one sdist, and no duplicates.
- A hand-written manifest listing `other-9.9.9-*.whl` and `*.tar.gz` under `pypi/demo` passes digest verification and is uploaded, because `compare` reports them missing.
- The manifest is a fully trusted input here: the envelope digest is computed from the manifest itself and pinned by nothing external. Re-running the `inventory` name and version predicate in `validate_distributions` closes it.

**F5. `git show -s --format=%ct HEAD` (Low, PLAUSIBLE).**
- `access.rs:369`: with `log.showSignature=true` and a signed HEAD, git prints gpg lines to stdout. `parse::<u64>` then fails, and every PyPI build, sealed or not, fails with a VcsError. Adding `--no-show-signature` avoids it.
- HEAD is the release source at this point. `validate_intent` (`capability.rs:~260-290`) re-derives the intent and requires it equal to the received one, whose source is the observed HEAD commit. `recheck_trust` runs before each effect. `build-python` goes through the same validation.

**Checked and found fine**
- **Version matching:** `render()` is used identically in `python_publishes`, `seal_distributions`, `sealed_files` and the cache key, so the string comparison is consistent. A mismatched manifest version or roster fails closed with `MismatchedDistributionRoster`. Sealing is all or none, and a partial or stray set is rejected.
- **Paths:** `resolve_asset_path` allows a single `Normal` component, rejects symlinks and non-files, and checks canonical containment. Verify and sealing both use it.
- **Collisions:** binary slot names and Python filenames are checked for duplicates together in `validate_distributions`, so a collision fails closed.
- **Digests:** `ArtifactDigest` is bare lowercase hex, matching the index's sha256 format.
- **Envelope:** the `sealable` relaxation only affects the `(slots empty, digest Some)` arm. A Python-less, slot-less intent is still rejected (test at `artifact.rs:~887`). No other consumer of `artifact_manifest_digest` or `artifact_slots.is_empty()` was missed.
- **Execute match:** the or-pattern guard in `release.rs:~574` applies to both alternatives. A Python-only intent with a manifest that has no distributions gets E232. A manifest without a directory errors.
- **Compare ordering:** differing files are checked before yanked in preflight and publish, and the `differing` and `yanked` checks happen before any upload.
- **Template gating:** `execute` needs `build-python` success, or `skipped` only when `has_python != 'true'`. A failed `build-python` blocks `execute`, and `release != 'true'` blocks it too. The `has_python` jq matches the intent JSON shape (`id.role.kind == "registryPublish"`, `id.package` starting `pypi/`), and the `python-dist` download and the `--seal-python` condition are consistent.
- **Env scrub:** `run_build_argv` still removes the credential variables through `RELEASE_CREDENTIALS`. `env SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=… python3` resolves through the same PATH as before.

**Notes, not defects**
- The `is_wheel` and `is_sdist` helpers are duplicated in `artifact.rs` and `pypi_files.rs`. The model copy accepts only `.tar.gz` for an sdist, while `dist_filename_parts` also accepts zip, bz2 and xz. AGENTS.md prefers one copy.
- A fresh workflow run after a partial upload rebuilds every file, and the strict compare then raises E307 for any non-bit-identical file. The legacy unsealed path tolerated that. This follows the spec text, but it narrows the "complete a partly uploaded release" behaviour from the previous commit when a build is not reproducible. "Re-run failed jobs" reuses the sealed artifact and is unaffected.
- `build_python_distributions` builds twice into one directory if one package has two PyPI registry publishes.

- **Version matching:** `render()` is used identically in `python_publishes`, `seal_distributions`, `sealed_files` and the cache key, so the string comparison is consistent. A mismatched manifest version or roster fails closed with `MismatchedDistributionRoster`. Sealing is all or none, and a partial or stray set is rejected.
- **Paths:** `resolve_asset_path` allows a single `Normal` component, rejects symlinks and non-files, and checks canonical containment. Verify and sealing both use it.
- **Collisions:** binary slot names and Python filenames are checked for duplicates together in `validate_distributions`, so a collision fails closed.
- **Digests:** `ArtifactDigest` is bare lowercase hex, matching the index's sha256 format.
- **Envelope:** the `sealable` relaxation only affects the `(slots empty, digest Some)` arm. A Python-less, slot-less intent is still rejected (test at `artifact.rs:~887`). No other consumer of `artifact_manifest_digest` or `artifact_slots.is_empty()` was missed.
- **Execute match:** the or-pattern guard in `release.rs:~574` applies to both alternatives. A Python-only intent with a manifest that has no distributions gets E232. A manifest without a directory errors.
- **Compare ordering:** differing files are checked before yanked in preflight and publish, and the `differing` and `yanked` checks happen before any upload.
- **Template gating:** `execute` needs `build-python` success, or `skipped` only when `has_python != 'true'`. A failed `build-python` blocks `execute`, and `release != 'true'` blocks it too. The `has_python` jq matches the intent JSON shape (`id.role.kind == "registryPublish"`, `id.package` starting `pypi/`), and the `python-dist` download and the `--seal-python` condition are consistent.
- **Env scrub:** `run_build_argv` still removes the credential variables through `RELEASE_CREDENTIALS`. `env SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=… python3` resolves through the same PATH as before.

**Notes, not defects**
- The `is_wheel` and `is_sdist` helpers are duplicated in `artifact.rs` and `pypi_files.rs`. The model copy accepts only `.tar.gz` for an sdist, while `dist_filename_parts` also accepts zip, bz2 and xz. AGENTS.md prefers one copy.
- A fresh workflow run after a partial upload rebuilds every file, and the strict compare then raises E307 for any non-bit-identical file. The legacy unsealed path tolerated that. This follows the spec text, but it narrows the "complete a partly uploaded release" behaviour from the previous commit when a build is not reproducible. "Re-run failed jobs" reuses the sealed artifact and is unaffected.
